problem: An original autonomous email included internal editorial labels and a role-only personalization, yet passed message composer quality with score 1.0 and was provider-sent.
root_cause: A generic editorial-council trusted-advisor checklist for longform content was applied verbatim to one-to-one commercial email; existing quality gate checked role/company anchoring but not a meaningful unique contact reason or natural-language quality.
failed_approaches: Treat role and company as a unique observed reason for mailing
Expose editorial hypothesis and limitation disclaimers in recipient copy
Treat score 1.0 as proof of human readability
fix: Separate email-intent instruction by channel, add deterministic human-copy and substantive-evidence guard inside original composer, retain original send permissions and independent provider verification.
verification_required: exact-head required/backend tests including failed production case
independently verified next eligible copy outcome; no resend
boundaries: No new scheduler, sender, queue or model service
No claim that PR equals deployed fix
Explicit consent/legal basis remains separately required under existing rules
No provider resend of already completed action
prevention_rule: A score 1.0 cannot bypass observed prospect-specific reasons and natural language; no internal editorial labels, no invented buying intent. Keep original consent and provider truth gates.
